physics_goals.value: Measure direct CP violation in neutral kaon decays to two pions (the parameter Re(ε′/ε)) to determine whether CP violation arises directly in the decay process itself, not only in K⁰-K̄⁰ mixing

summary.plain: NA48 was a CERN experiment that ran from the late 1990s to the mid-2000s, confirming that nature's matter-antimatter asymmetry (CP violation) can arise directly inside a kaon's decay, not just from how kaons mix. It was the direct predecessor of NA62 at the same underground cavern.
summary.technical: Fixed-target kaon experiment in the ECN3 cavern of the CERN SPS North Area (approved 1991), using concurrent KS/KL beams to measure direct CP violation (Re(ε′/ε) = (14.7 ± 2.2) × 10⁻⁴, combining 1997-1999 and 2001 data). Continued as NA48/2 (2003-2004) studying charged-kaon CP violation and rare decays before the programme's infrastructure was reused by its successor, NA62.

unique_capabilities.value: Simultaneous, nearly-collinear KS and KL beams tagged by the protons that produced the KS component, allowing all four CP-violation-sensitive decay modes to be measured concurrently and many systematic effects to cancel
